ingredients.name: Split chana (gram) lentils
ingredients.notes: soaked for at least 6 hours or overnight, then strained

ingredients.name: Fresh or frozen raw prawns
ingredients.notes: shell-on small prawns authentic; large peeled prawns work too

ingredients.name: Oil for frying
ingredients.notes: vegetable or coconut oil, about 5cm deep in wok

steps.instruction: Soak chana lentils in water for at least 6 hours or overnight until soft enough to smash between fingers. Strain well — do not add any water to the processor.
Place strained lentils in a food processor with garlic, chilli flakes, chilli powder, salt, red onion, green chillies, and curry leaves. Blend to a thick paste without adding water.

Wet your hands with water. Take a small handful of paste, form into a ball, flatten slightly, and press one prawn firmly into the centre so it holds during frying. Repeat with remaining paste and prawns.
Heat oil in a wok to 200°C (400°F). Test readiness by placing a wooden chopstick in the oil — if bubbles sizzle from it immediately, the oil is ready.
Fry vade in small batches of 3, splashing oil over the top with a spoon until lightly golden and the prawn is cooked through, about 3–4 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack or paper towel.
Serve topped with tamarind sauce or hot sauce and salad vegetables (shredded cabbage, grated carrot, spring onions, tomato).

notes: Hugely popular street food in Colombo and Negombo. Recipe by Dan Toombs (The Curry Guy), learned on location in Sri Lanka Jan 2022. Authentic versions use small shell-on prawns. Soak time (6h) not included in total_time_min. Note: chana dal = split chickpea lentils, different from ing_lentil_green — update taxonomy.
